sources: FAOSTAT consumer price indices (general and food, 2015 = 100, monthly; https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/CP), fetched 2026-10-25; Brent: FRED MCOILBRENTEU (monthly average, US$), fetched 2026-10-25
method: one model per price kind and horizon, pooled across countries, predicting how far the next h months' annualised log rate departs from the last 12 months'; candidates ridge, median (LAD) linear, gradient-boosted trees (squared loss, clipped target) and the LAD/trees average; rolling-origin backtest every 3 months, linear models refitted at each origin and trees every 6 months, on outcomes known by then; the best candidate per kind and horizon is used, naive where none beats it; 90% band = forecast + pooled 5%/95% quantiles of error / (the country's own 36-month volatility of seasonally adjusted monthly changes x sqrt h)
exclusions: Lebanon, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Venezuela and Zimbabwe are never trained on and get the naive rule; so does any country-month with 12-month inflation above 50% (or below -33%). Those rows are scored apart (the fragile column), not in the pooled skill.
reading: The pooled model beats naive at 10 of 10 kind-horizon cells. Winner by cell: the gradient-boosted trees 6, the average of the median linear model and the trees 4. Skill runs from +0.100 (all 6 mo) to +0.180 (food 6 mo): the model cuts the naive rule's mean absolute miss by that share. It helps in both groups: +0.095 to +0.243 where inflation was above 10% at the origin, +0.089 to +0.182 elsewhere. Out-of-sample 90% band coverage is 83% to 90% across cells. At 12 months the shortfall sits in a few origin years (lowest: all 2021 47%, food 2021 60%, all 2020 72%), when outcomes ran beyond the errors the band had seen before; the skill also varies by year, so the gain is an average over calm and turbulent spells.
